claim.pdf_says: ACCEPT screen-name-1 / Format 3 AT phrase, printed as a BRACE WITH CHOICE INDICATORS: '[ AT { |   LINE NUMBER { identifier-3 / integer-1 }   ,   { COLUMN / COL } NUMBER { identifier-4 / integer-2 }   | } ]'. Verified by cropping and enlarging spec_p607.png: immediately inside the tall brace that follows AT there is a single vertical bar on the left, and a matching single vertical bar immediately inside the closing brace on the right. There are NO brackets around the individual LINE / COLUMN rows.
claim.why_it_matters: The choice-indicator bars are dropped and each alternative is instead wrapped in a fabricated bracket. Per 5.2.6.4 bars inside a BRACE mean 'one or more of the enclosed alternatives, each at most once, in any order' -- so ACCEPT ... AT LINE NUMBER n COLUMN NUMBER m is legal. The markdown's brace-of-two-optional-brackets reads as 'exactly one of (optional LINE phrase) or (optional COLUMN phrase)', which forbids specifying BOTH LINE and COLUMN in one ACCEPT. The identical construct on page 640 (DISPLAY Format 2) DOES preserve the bars, which proves the intended transcription and confirms 607 is the defect.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the printed glyphs at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v607/spec_p607.png), cropped and enlarged 2x-5x.

1) LEFT EDGE (crop of orig px 330-730 x 570-1110, 3x): reading left to right the figure prints a tall '[' -- unmistakable, it has the horizontal serif feet at top and bottom -- then 'AT', then a tall '{' brace, then IMMEDIATELY inside that brace a single tall PLAIN VERTICAL LINE with flat ends and NO serifs. A bracket glyph in this typeface always carries the top/bottom feet (the outer '[' two glyphs to its left proves it); this line has none. It is a choice-indicator bar, not a bracket. The 'LINE NUMBER' row then begins directly with underlined LINE -- there is NO bracket opening around that row.

2) RIGHT EDGE (crop of orig px 1300-1560 x 570-1110, 5x): reading left to right there are exactly three tall glyphs: a serif-less plain vertical bar, then a '}' (visible mid-height pinch/point), then a ']' (horizontal serif feet). No per-row bracket closes before the bar. So the printed structure is exactly '[ AT { | <LINE row> <COLUMN row> | } ]' -- one bar just inside the opening brace, one matching bar just inside the closing brace, with the two rows vertically stacked between them and no individual brackets.

3) The claim quotes the markdown VERBATIM: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25263 is character-for-character the LaTeX string in the claim. No misquotation.

4) The semantic difference is real and normative. Per 5.2.6.4 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 2700): 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. When enclosed by braces, one or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative shall be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' The PDF therefore permits LINE alone, COLUMN alone, or BOTH in either order. The markdown replaces this with a plain brace (5.2.6.3 -- exactly one alternative selected) whose two alternatives are each a bracket (5.2.6.2 -- optional). That reads as 'select exactly one of (optional LINE phrase) or (optional COLUMN phrase)', which makes ACCEPT scr AT LINE NUMBER 5 COLUMN NUMBER 10 syntactically ILLEGAL. It also degenerates: selecting either alternative and then omitting its optional content yields a bare 'AT' with no operand. Both readings are wrong.

5) Internal corroboration on the same page defeats any 'harmless reformatting' defence. General rules 15-17 (lines 25382-25386) read: '15) The LINE and COLUMN phrases give the position ... Identifier-3 and identifier-4 are evaluated once at the start of execution of the statement.' '16) If the LINE phrase is not specified, the screen record starts on line 1.' '17) If the COLUMN phrase is not specified, the screen record starts in column 1.' GR 15 evaluates BOTH identifier-3 and identifier-4 in one statement execution, and GRs 16 and 17 give each phrase an INDEPENDENT default. That is coherent only under the choice-indicator reading (each independently omissible, both may co-occur, at least one present when AT is written) and is directly contradicted by the markdown's mutually exclusive reading.

6) External corroboration: the claim's page-640 cross-check holds. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26499-26504 transcribe the identical DISPLAY Format 2 AT phrase as an ASCII box-drawing figure that DOES preserve the bars -- '⎧|                ... |⎫' with the bars immediately inside the braces and no per-row brackets. Same construct, correct transcription there, defective transcription on 607.

I attempted and failed to refute on every available ground: the bars are not present-but-reflowed (I looked at the glyphs and there are no bars anywhere in the markdown figure); the difference is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or formatting (bracket/brace/bar are the standard's normative meta-language, defined in 5.2.6); the claim does not misquote either source; and the meaning demonstrably changes -- a construct the standard permits is rendered illegal.
verdict.corrected_description:
The finding is real and the claim's reading of the printed glyphs is accurate. Two refinements, neither of which weakens it:

(a) The claim's ASCII paraphrase of the PDF inserts a comma between the LINE row and the COLUMN row ('{ identifier-3 / integer-1 }   ,   { COLUMN / COL }'). No comma is printed. The two rows are simply stacked vertically inside the choice-indicator bars; the comma is only the claim author's line-layout separator and should not be read as spec text.

(b) The SAME figure carries a SECOND, identical defect that the claim does not mention. The ON EXCEPTION group printed immediately below the AT phrase is also enclosed in choice indicators -- cropping orig px 330-1420 x 1090-1250 shows a tall '[' then a plain serif-less vertical bar, the two stacked EXCEPTION rows, then a plain vertical bar, then ']'. That is '[ | ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1 / NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2 | ]'. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25265 transcribes it as a plain bracket with two stacked rows, dropping both bars. Per 5.2.6.4, bars inside BRACKETS mean 'zero or more of the enclosed alternatives, each at most once, in any order', so the PDF permits ON EXCEPTION alone, NOT ON EXCEPTION alone, BOTH in either order, or neither. The markdown's plain bracket reads as 'optional, choose exactly one', which wrongly forbids writing both handlers on one ACCEPT -- a form every COBOL statement admits. Page 640's DISPLAY Format 2 again preserves these bars ('⎡|  ON EXCEPTION ... |⎤'), confirming 607 is the defective page.

Correct transcription for specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25263 (AT phrase): outer BRACKET, then AT, then a BRACE whose contents are wrapped in a pair of choice-indicator bars, the bars enclosing two stacked alternatives -- 'LINE NUMBER { identifier-3 / integer-1 }' and '{ COLUMN / COL } NUMBER { identifier-4 / integer-2 }' -- with NO brackets around either alternative. Line 25265 (ON EXCEPTION) needs the same repair: a BRACKET enclosing a pair of choice-indicator bars around the two stacked EXCEPTION rows.

Compiler impact: the ACCEPT screen Format 3 AT phrase must accept LINE alone, COLUMN alone, and LINE followed by COLUMN (and, per 'in any order', COLUMN followed by LINE), with the missing phrase defaulting to 1 per general rules 16 and 17.
